issues.passage: Editors praised her fabrication of the timeline for matching every court record exactly.
issues.why: Definition includes manufacturing/making as well as falsehood. "Fabrication of the timeline" is a defensible manufacturing/construction reading, and praise for exact match to court records fits that sense. A student who knows both definitions could rightly accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: Investigators concluded that the signature on the form was a fabrication.
wrongPassages: Her careful fabrication of each citation against the archive left the bibliography flawless.
Their fabrication on the paper earned both coauthors equal credit in the journal.
Demolition crews finished the fabrication of the old wing before noon.

issues.passage: With an earnest glance at her phone, she promised help and never followed up.
issues.why: "Earnest glance" is natural, correct use of earnest = sincere and serious. The broken promise is only a pragmatic follow-on; it does not make the adjective a misuse. wrongPassages[0] ("earnest quip") is also AMBIGUOUS—a quip offered sincerely can still be called earnest—so all three wrongs are rewritten as clear misuses.

fix.correctPassage: Her earnest appeal for more lab time persuaded even the skeptical dean.
wrongPassages: He filed an earnest for early dismissal and left before the vote was called.
Engineers measured the bridge's earnest before certifying it for heavy traffic.
They dismissed the proposal as too earnest for the department's limited budget.
